purpose: The cleanup packet's exact-ID set is incomplete. This artifact re-derives it on measured ground so the deletion packet can be rebuilt. IT AUTHORIZES NOTHING: no row may be deleted on the strength of this file. Deletion still requires a separate, independently reviewed packet and explicit PM authorization.

supersedes.relationship: strict superset — v2 adds 31 ids and removes none

reproducibility_check.claim: The packet's stale classifier reproduces its own published checksum against current data, so the delta below is a genuine classifier correction and not data drift.
reproducibility_check.method: encode(sha256(string_agg(id::text, ',' ORDER BY id::text)::bytea), 'hex') over the v1 predicate — the same construction classifier.sql documents

checksums.note: sha256 of the sorted id::text list joined by ','. Anyone can re-derive the full id list from the published predicate and verify against these.

predicate_of_record.semantics: returns NULL for a legitimate pick, else a reason code; fixture set is `IS NOT NULL`, legitimate set is `IS NULL`
predicate_of_record.why_not_an_or_chain: A bare OR-chain is three-valued: metadata->>'eventName' is SQL NULL when the key is absent, so `false OR NULL` is NULL for 411 of 107,858 rows, and `WHERE NOT (predicate)` drops them from BOTH sides. Any rebuilt deletion packet MUST use this CASE form or an explicit captured id list.

exclusion_classes.note: These three classes have materially different deletion risk and MUST NOT be merged into a single deletion scope.

ci.description: CI / proof-harness fixtures. Self-identifying via proof_issue / proofRunId metadata keys, db-smoke event names, UTV2 selection or event prefixes, per-run [utv2-<issue>-<run>] tags, or the purely synthetic t1-proof / canary-proof sources.

qa_demo.description: Operator QA and dry-run rows: 5 'Command Center QA 202606' (submittedBy codex-command-center-p…) and 1 'STAFF-ONLY DRY RUN'. Not CI fixtures — human-driven demo traffic.
qa_demo.deletion_recommendation: EXCLUDE FROM ANY DELETION SCOPE. These 6 picks are the sole source of command_center_delivery_mappings entanglement (all 16 rows), and command_center_delivery_mappings is one of the two tables with no CREATE TABLE in the migration ledger. Deleting them would mutate a table whose DDL the repo cannot replay. Exclude from reporting only.

dependent_table_recount.consistency_check: pick_offer_snapshots 20 (fixture) + 173 (legitimate) = 193 = the packet's stated table total, so the reclassification is internally consistent.

packet_claims_now_invalid: relationships.md section 2: 'command_center_delivery_mappings pointing at a fixture pick — 0'. Actually 16.

relationships.md section 4 deletion order: lists `pick_offer_snapshots (0) not in scope` and `command_center_delivery_mappings (0) not in scope`. Both are now in scope and must be sequenced before `picks`.
relationships.md section 4 total: 518,037 rows across 11 tables. Understated — the corrected scope adds 261 dependent rows across 8 tables plus 31 picks and 31 submissions.

delta_ids_missing_from_packet.description: Exact ids the stale packet classifies as LEGITIMATE and the corrected classifier classifies as FIXTURE. Every one was inspected individually. None is a real pick.

rebuild_guidance_for_the_deletion_packet: Re-derive the id set from reporting.pick_fixture_reason, not from the stale inventory.json.

Scope deletion to class `ci` only (100,270 picks). Hold `qa_demo` (6) and `junk` (2) out — the qa_demo rows alone drag in all 16 command_center_delivery_mappings rows, in a table with no CREATE TABLE in the migration ledger.
Add pick_offer_snapshots (20) to the dependency-resolved order; relationships.md omits it as out of scope.

The blocking conditions relationships.md identified are unchanged and still governing: settlement_records is DELETE-blocked by trigger trg_settlement_records_immutable (35,923 rows now), audit_log is immutable, settlement_records.corrects_id is RESTRICT and needs depth-first ordering, and pick_reviews is NO ACTION and must be deleted explicitly.
Nothing in this artifact authorizes deletion. It exists so that when deletion IS authorized, it is authorized against a measured id set rather than a stale one.
